questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The academic content and how well the universities collab

Additional comments:

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. A lot of the information was given by the hosting university

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: difficult, because most off campus housing was community housing and they would rather have dutch speeking people than english.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: A bike is necessary to get around especially if you live off campus. It is also important to know that one can register in the municipality to get funding for ones housing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Very similar to the process from my own institute. They will send out a notice if you have to sign up for courses and when you should do it. The same goes for resits. Afterwards it will be confirmed if you are inroled or not.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Student service, IT-service, and the proffessors were also happy to help

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: very successful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: To make sure that you have gotten a confirmation when registrating to a course and do it in time

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took three MA courses and two BA courses. The acedemic level was greater than what I expected. Sometimes the two courses was too much when both had a large syllabus.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was more or likely the same, but I liked that all lectures were recorded

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I joined the gymnastics team at my host university and they have a lot of other clubs. I got a membership in their fitness center on campus. Also joined ESN (erasmus student network) and had some great experiences with them.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: travel to different cities on the weekend to see something other than wageningen. Amsterdam is a great place to go to and also Utrect.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There are no clubs in wageningen so you'll have to go other places like Utrecht.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: it was pretty easy, but dutch people are not so willing to speak english all the time, and it's difficult to learn their language, but fun.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: go to student associations, they host a lot of parties. Join ESN, and join a sport you like to socialize

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Language barrier and going to the hospital where only a few people know english.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Open minded, very social and a lot of cheese and bakeries

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: academic level is challenging, join a community housing if possible to socialize, remember to enjoy your time there

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get a dutch phone number

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: getting new friends and seeing experiencing a new country in i different way than regular travelling

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
